text:
The Avalanche are going to spend the next few months finding out who they are without Nathan MacKinnon, whose injury setback has him out roughly three months by the latest reports. If Wednesday is any sign, the answer is a team that still knows how to bury a struggling opponent. Colorado beat Montreal 6-0, deserved to win 76% of the time by our replays of every shot, and outshot the Canadiens 38 to 28.

It started with a Montreal mistake. Logan O'Connor poked home a loose puck at 9:43 of the first, seconds after what Karine Hains of The Hockey News described as a Noah Dobson giveaway. Artturi Lehkonen made it 2-0 thirty seconds into the second on a 47% chance set up by Cale Makar and Martin Necas. Then Devon Toews scored twice in the final 1:39 of the period, once on the power play and once at even strength, and the game was gone. Necas and Gabriel Landeskog added goals in the third. Makar finished with three assists in 24 minutes, Necas with a goal and two, and Brock Nelson, now the man filling MacKinnon's minutes at center, set up two more.

Mackenzie Blackwood did not need to be spectacular, but he was perfect: 28 saves, 2.38 goals better than the chances he faced. Jacob Fowler gave up six on 38 shots at the other end.

For Montreal, a team still settling in after acquiring Dylan Larkin from Detroit, the night got worse after the scoreboard stopped mattering. Kaiden Guhle left after a hit from Landeskog, and the Canadiens are already without Mike Matheson, Chris Kreider and Josh Anderson. The late-game scuffles that followed, with Florian Xhekaj inviting Landeskog to fight, drew pointed comments from the Avalanche captain afterward, per Corey Masisak of the Denver Post. Montreal ran up 39 penalty minutes. As Eric Engels of Sportsnet put it, the timing of the injuries is a major problem for a team already struggling. This was also the second time in eleven days Colorado beat them, after a 4-1 win on November 14.
headline: Without MacKinnon, the Avalanche still bury Montreal
